rows.description: A child who wins the school prize is mocked as a "show-off" by classmates and starts hiding good marks to fit in again.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Downplaying own success to stay liked [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager who gets selected for a national contest plays it down and jokes about it, afraid that pride will make friends turn cold and call them arrogant.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult feels a sting when a peer is praised and finds small faults to mention; envy and fear of being left behind turn admiration into criticism.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, fear, envy

rows.subtype: Team sniping at the promoted colleague [Observer]
rows.description: A manager sees a team quietly withdraw support from a newly promoted colleague; the group's comfort with equality is threatened when one person moves up.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A person notices their own envy, names it, and instead of undermining the achiever congratulates them and asks what the success shows about their own goals.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler is calmed by the lullaby and faces they know and is wary of strangers; familiarity signals safety, so the known simply feels better.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, calm, trust

rows.description: A child who found a tune odd at first begins to love it after hearing it many times at family functions; repeated contact alone raised the liking.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Warming to a classmate through daily contact [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager who disliked a new classmate at first likes them after seeing them daily in the same bus and class; simply being around makes people feel friendlier.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Familiar brand mistaken for a better one [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult picks the brand seen in countless adverts and believes it is good, when what they feel is familiarity, not quality.
